rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He found Muhammad poor and without property, then enriched him through Khadija.
rows.anchor: أي فقيرا لا مال لك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb عال يعيل means to become poor; Ahiha ibn al-Jallah uses it of a rich man becoming poor.
rows.anchor: عال الرجل يعيل عيلة : إذا افتقر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God made Muhammad content with the provision He gave him.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : فرضاك بما أعطاك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the enrichment as making Muhammad content with his provision.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : قنعك بالرزق

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says Muhammad was poor in spirit and God enriched his heart.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : ووجدك فقير النفس

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash takes عائلا to mean that Muhammad had dependents; Jarir's verse uses العائل for a poor person with dependents.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش : وجدك ذا عيال . دليله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says he was poor in arguments and proofs, then God enriched him with them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : وجدك فقيرا من الحجج والبراهين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God enriched him through conquests and the property of unbelievers granted to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أغناك بما فتح لك من الفتوح

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri objects to the conquest-and-spoils interpretation because the sura is Meccan and fighting was prescribed only in Medina.
rows.anchor: القشيري : وفي هذا نظر ؛ لأن السورة مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading is عائلا; Ibn al-Sumayqa reads عيلا with a doubled y, like طيب and هين.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة " عائلا " . وقرأ ابن السميقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human in this oath's answer means the unbeliever; on this reading the verse concerns deniers of resurrection.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب القسم ، وأراد بالإنسان : الكافر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported identification of the unbelieving human is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: قيل : هو الوليد بن المغيرة .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification of the unbelieving human is Kalda ibn Asid.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كلدة بن أسيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes the human as Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالإنسان آدم وذريته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators understand the best stature as human balance and uprightness in full youth: other creatures face down, while humans stand upright with articulate tongues and grasping hands and fingers.
rows.anchor: وهو اعتداله واستواء شبابه ، كذا قال عامة المفسرين .

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir describes humans as adorned with reason, responsive to commands, discerning, tall, and able to take food by hand.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : مزينا بالعقل ، مؤديا للأمر

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says no creation is more beautiful: humans possess life, knowledge, power, will, speech, hearing, sight, governance, and wisdom; the report that Adam was created upon God's image refers to such qualities, since God has no corporeal image.
rows.anchor: ابن العربي : ليس لله تعالى خلق أحسن من الإنسان ، فإن الله خلقه حيا عالما

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the version upon the Merciful's image cannot imply a particularized divine form; it must refer to meanings or qualities.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية [ على صورة الرحمن ] ومن أين تكون للرحمن صورة متشخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an anecdote, a Hanafi jurist held that a husband's oath to divorce unless his wife was more beautiful than the moon did not take effect, since humans are the most beautiful things; al-Mansur accepted his ruling.
rows.anchor: فقال له الرجل : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم : " والتين والزيتون . وطور سينين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows humans are God's most beautiful creation inside and out, with a finely composed head, chest, belly, sexual organs, hands, and legs.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدلك على أن الإنسان أحسن خلق الله باطنا وظاهرا ، جمال هيئة

rows.speaker: الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Philosophers call the human the microcosm because all that is in creation is gathered in the human.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قالت الفلاسفة : إنه العالم الأصغر ؛ إذ كل ما في المخلوقات جمع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus, has nineteen verses, and is the first revelation according to most commentators; Gabriel delivered its first five verses at Hira.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بإجماع ، وهي أول ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir ibn Abdullah says the first revelation was al-Muddaththir, chapter 74.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أول ما نزل " يا أيها المدثر " [ المدثر : 1 ]

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة الهمداني
rows.claim: Abu Maysara al-Hamdani says the Opening Sura was the first revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فاتحة الكتاب أول ما نزل . قاله أبو ميسرة الهمداني

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says the first revelation was the command to recite what God prohibited, from 6:151; al-Qurtubi calls the first-sura view correct.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : أول ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says true dreams were the beginning of revelation, then Gabriel came and delivered the opening verses; al-Bukhari transmits this report.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الرؤيا الصادقة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In the two Sahih collections, Aisha recounts true dreams, retreat at Hira, Gabriel's three forceful embraces after Muhammad says he cannot read, and the first five verses.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عنها قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Abu Raja al-Ataridi recalls Abu Musa teaching this sura in circles at the Basra mosque and saying it was the first sura revealed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء العطاردي : وكان أبو موسى الأشعري يطوف علينا في هذا المسجد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha's reported revelation order after this sura is Nun wa-l-Qalam, al-Muddaththir, then al-Duha; al-Mawardi cites the report.
rows.anchor: وروت عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها أول سورة أنزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، ثم بعدها

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says the first revelation extended through ما لم يعلم; Muhammad grieved, Gabriel affirmed he was God's prophet, and after Muhammad asked to be covered and cooled, al-Muddaththir was revealed.
rows.anchor: وعن الزهري : أول ما نزل سورة : " اقرأ باسم ربك - إلى قوله - ما لم يعلم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read what has been revealed of the Qur'an, beginning in God's name; al-Qurtubi takes this to mean saying the basmala at the start of each sura.
rows.anchor: ومعنى " اقرأ باسم ربك " أي اقرأ ما أنزل إليك من القرآن مفتتحا باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi in باسم ربك is in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: فمحل الباء من " باسم ربك " النصب على الحال .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another analysis makes bi mean على; the recited object is omitted, so the sense is to recite the Qur'an and begin it in God's name.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الباء بمعنى على ، أي اقرأ على اسم ربك .

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say God's name here means the Qur'an and bi is extra, as in 23:20; al-Rai's verse about not reading suras with bi also supports this usage.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : اسم ربك هو القرآن ، فهو يقول : " اقرأ باسم ربك " أي اسم ربك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is simply to remember God's name: Muhammad is commanded to begin recitation by naming God.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى " اقرأ باسم ربك " أي اذكر اسمه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human means the son of Adam.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : " خلق الإنسان " يعني ابن آدم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alaq is the plural of alaqa, a clotted blood; once blood flows it is called spilt blood.
rows.anchor: " من علق " أي من دم ، جمع علقة ، والعلقة الدم الجامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural form is used because al-insan is generic: all humans are created from clots after the drop of semen.
rows.anchor: فذكره بلفظ الجمع ؛ لأنه أراد بالإنسان الجمع ، وكلهم خلقوا من علق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clot is a moist piece of blood, named for clinging to what it touches; when it dries it is no longer called alaqa.
rows.anchor: والعلقة : قطعة من دم رطب ، سميت بذلك لأنها تعلق لرطوبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem describes blood from the heart's vital vein as علق, illustrating the word's sense of blood.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : تركناه يخر على يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity is singled out for honor by name.
rows.anchor: وخص الإنسان بالذكر تشريفا له .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the verse displays God's favor: He made humans from a lowly clot and brought them to upright, rational maturity.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد أن يبين قدر نعمته عليه ، بأن خلقه من علقة مهينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command confirms the first; that sentence is complete, and a new sentence begins with your Lord is most generous.
rows.anchor: " اقرأ " تأكيد ، وتم الكلام ، ثم استأنف فقال : " وربك الأكرم "

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the Most Generous as forbearing toward servants' ignorance and not hastening to punish them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : يعني الحليم عن جهل العباد ، فلم يعجل بعقوبتهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the ordinary sense generous, since the blessings just mentioned demonstrate God's generosity.
rows.anchor: والأول أشبه بالمعنى ، لأنه لما ذكر ما تقدم من نعمه ، دل بها على كرمه .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading of the phrase addresses Muhammad: read, and your Lord will help and teach you even though you cannot read.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " اقرأ وربك " أي اقرأ يا محمد وربك يعينك ويفهمك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss takes al-akram to mean the One who overlooks servants' ignorance.
rows.anchor: و " الأكرم " بمعنى المتجاوز عن جهل العباد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen means script and writing: God taught humans to write with a pen.
rows.anchor: " الذي علم بالقلم " يعني الخط والكتابة ، أي علم الإنسان الخط بالقلم .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says, as transmitted by Said, that the pen is a great divine blessing; without it religion would not stand and life would not be sound.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد عن قتادة قال : القلم نعمة من الله تعالى عظيمة ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen displays God's complete generosity: teaching people what they did not know and moving them from ignorance's darkness to knowledge's light.
rows.anchor: فدل على كمال كرمه سبحانه ، بأنه علم عباده ما لم يعلموا ، ونقلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing records knowledge, preserves wisdom and earlier reports, and transmits revealed books; without it the affairs of religion and worldly life would not remain sound.
rows.anchor: وما دونت العلوم ، ولا قيدت الحكم ، ولا ضبطت أخبار الأولين ومقالاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen is called qalam because it cuts, as in trimming a fingernail.
rows.anchor: وسمي قلما لأنه يقلم ، أي يقطع ، ومنه تقليم الظفر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A modern poet likens the ink-stained pen tip to an old man courting a young woman and says it raises written pages to God.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الشعراء المحدثين يصف القلم : فكأنه والحبر يخضب رأسه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar asked the Prophet whether he should write the hadith he heard; the Prophet said yes, since God taught by the pen.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمر قال : يا رسول الله ، أأكتب ما أسمع منك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports from Abu Umar that God created four things with His hand, then told the other animals to be: the pen, Throne, Garden of Eden, and Adam.
rows.anchor: وروى مجاهد عن أبي عمر قال : خلق الله عز وجل أربعة أشياء بيده

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the one taught by the pen is Adam, the first to write.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه آدم عليه السلام ؛ لأنه أول من كتب ، قاله كعب الأحبار .

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the one taught by the pen is Idris, the first to write.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه إدريس ، وهو أول من كتب . قاله الضحاك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view includes everyone who writes, since all writing is taught by God; this gathers His favors in creating and teaching humanity.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه أدخل كل من كتب بالقلم ؛ لأنه ما علم إلا بتعليم الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra says God wrote in a book held above the Throne that His mercy overcomes His wrath.
rows.anchor: صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حديث أبي هريرة ، قال : ( لما خلق الله الخلق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report established from the Prophet says the first created thing was the pen; God commanded it to write what would occur through the Resurrection, kept in the Record above His Throne.
rows.anchor: وثبت عنه عليه السلام أنه قال : ( أول ما خلق الله : القلم ، فقال له اكتب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: An authentic report from Ibn Masud says that after forty-two nights an angel shapes the embryo, creates its faculties, and writes its sex, term, and provision according to God's decree; the angel leaves with the page, and the verse names the recording guardians.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح من حديث ابن مسعود : أنه

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars distinguish three pens: God's first pen, commanded to write; angels' pens for decrees, events, and deeds; and human pens for speech and practical needs.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا : فالأقلام في الأصل ثلاثة : القلم الأول : الذي خلقه الله بيده

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars say writing has many virtues and belongs to البيان, a form of expression particular to human beings.
rows.anchor: وفي الكتابة فضائل جمة . والكتابة من جملة البيان ، والبيان مما اختص به الآدمي .

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars say Arabs knew writing little, and Muhammad least of all; being kept from it strengthened his miracle and proof, as discussed in al-Ankabut.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا : كانت العرب أقل الخلق معرفة بالكتاب ، وأقل العرب معرفة به المصطفى

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: A report attributed through Ibn Masud to the Prophet says not to house women in upper rooms or teach them writing; al-Qurtubi does not state a grading.
rows.anchor: وروى حماد بن سلمة عن الزبير بن عبد السلام ، عن أيوب بن عبد الله الفهري

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Scholars explain the warning against upper rooms by saying women might look out at men, creating temptation rather than concealment; they cite the saying that women are best off unseen by men and not seeing men.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا : وإنما حذرهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك ، لأن في إسكانهن الغرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says writing may enable women to correspond with men they desire; writing acts as an eye for the absent and a trace of the hand, voicing thoughts beyond speech, so the Prophet sought to cut off temptation and protect hearts.
rows.anchor: وكذلك تعليم الكتابة ربما كانت سببا للفتنة ، وذلك إذا علمت الكتابة كتبت إلى من تهوى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view identifies the human taught as Adam, whom God taught the names of everything in every language, as in 2:31.
rows.anchor: قيل : " الإنسان " هنا آدم عليه السلام . علمه أسماء كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam named what he had been taught before the angels, demonstrating his rank and prophethood, establishing God's proof, and leading the angels to obey when they witnessed God's power and command.
rows.anchor: وذكره آدم للملائكة كما علمه . وبذلك ظهر فضله ، وتبين قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's descendants inherited and transmitted this knowledge from generation to generation and people to people.
rows.anchor: ثم توارثت ذلك ذريته خلفا بعد سلف ، وتناقلوه قوما عن قوم .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the human as Muhammad, citing God's statement that He taught him what he did not know; on this view the teaching is future because this was among the earliest revelations.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " الإنسان " هنا الرسول محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم . دليله قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A general interpretation takes human to mean humanity, since people emerge from their mothers knowing nothing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو عام لقوله تعالى : " والله أخرجكم من بطون أمهاتكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says this verse, or the entire sura, came down about Abu Jahl when he prohibited Muhammad from praying.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنه نزل في أبي جهل . وقيل : نزلت السورة كلها في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the entire sura concerned Abu Jahl, it would not all be among the earliest revelations; alternatively, the first five verses came early and the rest later, then God ordered the later material joined to them, as with 2:281.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خمس آيات من أولها أول ما نزلت ، ثم نزلت البقية في شأن أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla means truly, since nothing precedes it here.
rows.anchor: و " كلا " بمعنى حقا ؛ إذ ليس قبله شيء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human who transgresses here is Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: والإنسان هنا أبو جهل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgression is exceeding the limit in disobedience.
rows.anchor: والطغيان : مجاوزة الحد في العصيان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cause is seeing himself as self-sufficient, with wealth and abundance.
rows.anchor: " أن رآه " أي لأن رأى نفسه استغنى ، أي صار ذا مال وثروة .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, via Abu Salih, reports that Abu Jahl asked Muhammad for Meccan mountains of gold so the polytheists might become rich, transgress, and abandon their religion for his; Gabriel offered to grant it if they wished, with punishment like the Table's people if they still rejected faith, but Muhammad refrained, knowing they would not accept.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح عنه ، قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية وسمع بها المشركون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Abu Jahl saw himself as self-sufficient through his clan, supporters, and helpers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : " أن رآه استغنى " بالعشيرة والأنصار والأعوان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal lām is omitted from an raahu, as in the example that people transgress when they see their wealth.
rows.anchor: وحذف اللام من قوله " أن رآه " كما يقال : إنكم لتطغون إن رأيتم غناكم .

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains that ra'a takes a subject and predicate, like verbs of supposition; Arabic can omit nafs in such constructions, as in I saw myself or thought myself leaving.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : لم يقل : رأى نفسه ، كما قيل : قتل نفسه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Hamid, and Qunbul from Ibn Kathir read the hamza short; the others lengthen it, which al-Qurtubi prefers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وقنبل عن ابن كثير " أن رآه استغنى " بقصر الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return of such a person is to his Lord, who will requite him.
rows.anchor: أي مرجع من هذا وصفه ، فنجازيه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ruj'a, al-marji, and al-ruju are verbal nouns for returning; ruj'a follows the fu'la pattern.
rows.anchor: والرجعى والمرجع والرجوع : مصادر ، يقال : رجع إليه رجوعا ومرجعا .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who forbids is Abu Jahl, and the servant he forbids is Muhammad; Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying, prompting these verses in astonishment.
rows.anchor: وهو أبو جهل " عبدا " وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم . فإن أبا جهل قال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An implied question asks whether the one forbidding prayer is safe from punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في الكلام حذف ، والمعنى : أمن هذا الناهي عن الصلاة من العقوبة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who forbids is Abu Jahl, and the servant he forbids is Muhammad; Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying, prompting these verses in astonishment.
rows.anchor: وهو أبو جهل " عبدا " وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم . فإن أبا جهل قال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An implied question asks whether the one forbidding prayer is safe from punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : في الكلام حذف ، والمعنى : أمن هذا الناهي عن الصلاة من العقوبة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing Abu Jahl, the verse asks whether, if Muhammad is guided and commands piety, the man forbidding his piety and prayer is not doomed.
rows.anchor: أي أرأيت يا أبا جهل إن كان محمد على هذه الصفة ، أليس ناهيه عن التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing Abu Jahl, the verse asks whether, if Muhammad is guided and commands piety, the man forbidding his piety and prayer is not doomed.
rows.anchor: أي أرأيت يا أبا جهل إن كان محمد على هذه الصفة ، أليس ناهيه عن التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl denied God's Book and turned away from belief.
rows.anchor: يعني أبا جهل كذب بكتاب الله عز وجل ، وأعرض عن الإيمان .

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra connects the clauses: the forbidden servant may be guided and command piety while the forbidding man denies and turns from the Reminder; the sequence marvels at this, then reproaches Abu Jahl for not knowing God sees and knows his act.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : المعنى " أرأيت الذي ينهى . عبدا إذا صلى " وهو على الهدى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another grammatical view makes each later أرأيت a substitute for the first, with ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى as the predicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كل واحد من " أرأيت " بدل من الأول . و " ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى " الخبر .

rows.anchor: وقيل : كل واحد من " أرأيت " بدل من الأول . و " ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى " الخبر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is that Abu Jahl must stop harming Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي أبو جهل عن أذاك يا محمد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means seizing the forelock and humiliating him.
rows.anchor: " لنسفعا " أي لنأخذن " بالناصية " فلنذلنه .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view places the seizure at the Resurrection: he will be taken by the forelock, folded with his feet, and thrown into Hell, as in 55:41.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لنأخذن بناصيته يوم القيامة ، وتطوى مع قدميه ، ويطرح في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though directed at Abu Jahl, the verse teaches everyone and warns anyone who refuses obedience or prevents others from it.
rows.anchor: فالآية - وإن كانت في أبي جهل - فهي عظة للناس ، وتهديد لمن يمتنع

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Lexicographers say safa'tu means to seize something and pull it hard; a cited poem uses سافع for one catching a horse by its forelock.
rows.anchor: وأهل اللغة يقولون : سفعت بالشيء : إذا قبضت عليه وجذبته جذبا شديدا .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derivation connects the word to fire or sun darkening the face; a cited line describes blackened stones beneath a cooking pot.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو مأخوذ من سفعته النار والشمس : إذا غيرت وجهه إلى حال تسويد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nasiyah is the hair at the front of the head, and can stand for the whole person, as in calling someone a blessed forelock.
rows.anchor: والناصية : شعر مقدم الرأس . وقد يعبر بها عن جملة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forelock is singled out because Arabs seize it when they want to abase and humiliate someone.
rows.anchor: وخص الناصية بالذكر على عادة العرب فيمن أرادوا إذلاله وإهانته

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines safa as a forceful pull, meaning that Abu Jahl will be dragged by his forelock into the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد : السفع : الجذب بشدة ، أي لنجرن بناصيته إلى النار .

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes safa as striking, specifically slapping the face; al-Qurtubi says the senses converge in blows during the seizure followed by dragging to Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل : السفع الضرب ، أي لنلطمن وجهه . وكله متقارب المعنى .
